tools.name: get_project_info
tools.description: Get Godot project metadata including name, version, viewport settings, renderer, and autoloads

tools.name: get_filesystem_tree
tools.description: Get the project's file/directory tree with optional filtering by extension (e.g. *.gd, *.tscn)

tools.name: search_files
tools.description: Search for files by name using fuzzy matching or glob patterns

query.description: Search query (fuzzy match or glob pattern)

tools.name: search_in_files
tools.description: Search for text content inside project files (grep-like). Searches through GDScript, scenes, resources, shaders, and other text files. Skips addons/ and .godot/ directories.

query.description: Text to search for (plain text or regex pattern)

file_type.description: Filter by file extension (e.g. 'gd', 'tscn'). Default: all text files

tools.name: get_project_settings
tools.description: Read project.godot settings by section or specific key

tools.name: set_project_setting
tools.description: Set a project setting value (e.g. viewport size, main scene). Saves to project.godot via the editor API.

value.description: Value to set. Strings are auto-parsed for Vector2, bool, int, float.

tools.name: uid_to_project_path
tools.description: Convert a Godot UID (uid://...) to a project resource path (res://...)

tools.name: project_path_to_uid
tools.description: Convert a project resource path (res://...) to its UID (uid://...)

tools.name: add_autoload
tools.description: Add an autoload (singleton) to the project. The script/scene will be auto-loaded when the project starts.

path.description: Path to the script or scene file (e.g. 'res://scripts/autoload/game_manager.gd')

tools.name: remove_autoload
tools.description: Remove an autoload (singleton) from the project settings

tools.name: get_scene_tree
tools.description: Get the live scene tree of the currently edited scene, showing all nodes, types, and hierarchy

max_depth.description: Max tree depth to return (-1 for unlimited)

tools.name: get_scene_file_content
tools.description: Read the raw .tscn file content of a scene

tools.name: create_scene
tools.description: Create a new scene file with a specified root node type

root_type.description: Root node type (default: Node2D). Examples: Node2D, Node3D, Control, CharacterBody2D

tools.name: open_scene
tools.description: Open a scene file in the Godot editor

tools.name: delete_scene
tools.description: Delete a scene file from the project

path.description: Path to the scene file to delete

tools.name: add_scene_instance
tools.description: Add an existing scene as a child node (instancing) in the current scene

scene_path.description: Path to the scene to instance (e.g. 'res://scenes/enemy.tscn')

tools.name: play_scene
tools.description: Run a scene in the Godot editor (main scene, current scene, or specific path)

tools.name: stop_scene
tools.description: Stop the currently playing scene

tools.name: save_scene
tools.description: Save the currently edited scene to disk

path.description: Optional path to save to (defaults to current scene path)

tools.name: get_scene_exports
tools.description: Get all @export variables from all scripted nodes in a scene file. Useful for inspecting configurable parameters without opening the scene.

tools.name: add_node
tools.description: Add a new node to the current scene. Supports built-in Godot types and script-defined classes (class_name).

type.description: Node type — built-in (e.g. 'Sprite2D', 'Camera2D') or script class_name (e.g. 'HoverDetector', 'StationBuilder')

tools.name: delete_node
tools.description: Delete a node from the current scene (supports undo)

node_path.description: Path to the node to delete

tools.name: duplicate_node
tools.description: Duplicate a node and all its children in the current scene

node_path.description: Path to the node to duplicate

tools.name: move_node
tools.description: Move/reparent a node to a new parent in the scene tree

node_path.description: Path to the node to move

new_parent_path.description: Path to the new parent node

tools.name: update_property
tools.description: Change a property on any node. Supports Vector2, Color, and other Godot types via string parsing.

value.description: New value. Strings are auto-parsed: 'Vector2(10,20)', 'Color(1,0,0)', '#ff0000', etc.

tools.name: get_node_properties
tools.description: Get all editor-visible properties of a node with their current values

tools.name: add_resource
tools.description: Add a resource (Shape2D, Material, Texture, etc.) to a node's property

property.description: Property to set the resource on (e.g. 'shape', 'material', 'texture')

resource_properties.description: Properties to set on the created resource

tools.name: set_anchor_preset
tools.description: Set a Control node's anchor preset (e.g. full_rect, center, top_left)

preset.description: Anchor preset name: top_left, top_right, bottom_left, bottom_right, center_left, center_top, center_right, center_bottom, center, left_wide, top_wide, right_wide, bottom_wide, vcenter_wide, hcenter_wide, full_rect

tools.name: rename_node
tools.description: Rename a node in the current scene

node_path.description: Path to the node to rename

tools.name: connect_signal
tools.description: Connect a signal from one node to a method on another node

method_name.description: Method name on target to call

tools.name: disconnect_signal
tools.description: Disconnect a signal connection between two nodes

tools.name: get_node_groups
tools.description: Get all groups a node belongs to (excludes internal groups starting with '_')

tools.name: set_node_groups
tools.description: Set the groups a node belongs to. Computes diff with current groups and adds/removes as needed.

groups.description: Desired list of group names (replaces current groups)

tools.name: find_nodes_in_group
tools.description: Find all nodes in the current scene that belong to a specific group

tools.name: list_scripts
tools.description: List all GDScript/C#/shader files in the project with class info

tools.name: read_script
tools.description: Read the full content of a GDScript file

tools.name: create_script
tools.description: Create a new GDScript file with optional content or auto-generated template

content.description: Full script content. If empty, generates a template.

extends.description: Base class (default: 'Node'). Only used for template generation.

class_name.description: Class name to add. Only used for template generation.

tools.name: edit_script
tools.description: Edit a script using search-and-replace, full content replacement, or line insertion

path.description: Path to the script to edit

insert_at_line.description: Line number to insert text at (0-indexed)

tools.name: attach_script
tools.description: Attach a GDScript to a node in the current scene

tools.name: validate_script
tools.description: Validate a GDScript file by attempting to compile it. Returns whether the script is valid. Use get_output_log or get_editor_errors for detailed error messages on failure.

path.description: Path to the script to validate (e.g. 'res://scripts/player.gd')

tools.name: get_open_scripts
tools.description: Get a list of scripts currently open in the Godot script editor

tools.name: get_editor_errors
tools.description: Get recent errors and stack traces from the Godot editor log

max_lines.description: Maximum log lines to scan for errors (default: 50)

tools.name: get_output_log
tools.description: Read the full Godot editor Output panel content. Unlike get_editor_errors which filters for errors only, this returns all output including print() statements and warnings.

max_lines.description: Maximum number of lines to return from the end (default: 100)

tools.name: get_editor_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a screenshot of the Godot editor's 2D/3D viewport

save_path.description: Optional res:// or user:// path to save the screenshot as PNG file (e.g. 'res://screenshot.png'). When provided, the image is saved to disk and the file path is returned instead of base64 data.

tools.name: get_game_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a single screenshot of the running game (requires a scene to be playing). Good for checking static visual state (UI layout, scene composition, colors). For verifying animations or movement, use capture_frames instead — a single screenshot cannot confirm whether an animation is playing.

save_path.description: Optional res:// or user:// path to save the screenshot as PNG file (e.g. 'res://screenshot.png'). When provided, the image is saved to disk and the file path is returned instead of base64 data.

tools.name: execute_editor_script
tools.description: Execute arbitrary GDScript code inside the Godot editor. Use _mcp_print() to output values.

code.description: GDScript code to execute. Use _mcp_print(value) to capture output. The code runs inside a run() function with access to the full editor API.

tools.name: clear_output
tools.description: Clear the Godot editor output panel

tools.name: get_signals
tools.description: Get all signals of a node, including current connections

node_path.description: Path to the node to inspect

tools.name: reload_plugin
tools.description: Reload the Godot MCP Pro plugin (disable/re-enable). Connection will briefly drop and auto-reconnect. NOTE: This does NOT reload GDScript preload() caches. If you changed GDScript command files, use execute_editor_script with 'EditorInterface.restart_editor(true)' instead for a full editor restart.

tools.name: reload_project
tools.description: Rescan the Godot project filesystem and reload changed scripts (no reconnection needed)

tools.name: compare_screenshots
tools.description: Compare two screenshots pixel-by-pixel and return a diff analysis. Returns changed pixel count, diff percentage, and a highlighted diff image. Useful for visual regression testing. Accepts file paths (res://, user://) or base64 PNG strings.

image_a.description: First image: file path (e.g. 'user://screenshot_a.png') or base64 PNG string

image_b.description: Second image: file path (e.g. 'user://screenshot_b.png') or base64 PNG string

threshold.description: Color difference threshold (0-255, default: 10). Pixels with max channel difference below this are considered identical.

tools.name: set_auto_dismiss
tools.description: Enable or disable automatic dismissal of blocking editor dialogs (e.g. 'Reload from disk?', 'Save changes?'). Enable this before operations that modify files externally, and disable when done. Disabled by default.

enabled.description: true to enable auto-dismiss, false to disable

tools.name: get_editor_camera
tools.description: Get the current 3D editor viewport camera position, rotation, and FOV. Use this to understand the current view before taking editor screenshots.

tools.name: set_editor_camera
tools.description: Move the 3D editor viewport camera to a specific position and orientation. Use this to frame a view before taking editor screenshots to validate changes visually.

look_at.description: Point to look at (overrides rotation_degrees if both set)

tools.name: simulate_key
tools.description: Simulate a keyboard key press or release in the running game. Use `duration` to hold a key for a set time (auto-releases after). Without duration: keys are NOT auto-released — you must explicitly call with pressed=false to release them.

pressed.description: true for press, false for release (default: true)

duration.description: Hold duration in seconds (e.g. 1.5). Key is pressed, held for this duration, then auto-released. Cannot be used with pressed=false.

tools.name: simulate_mouse_click
tools.description: Simulate a mouse button click at a position in the running game. By default sends both press and release (auto_release) so UI buttons work correctly.

pressed.description: true for press, false for release (default: true)

auto_release.description: Auto-send release after press so buttons fire (default: true). Set false for drag operations.

tools.name: simulate_mouse_move
tools.description: Simulate mouse movement in the running game. Use x/y for absolute viewport positioning (UI interaction), or relative_x/relative_y for relative motion (camera rotation in 3D games, FPS-style look). For 3D camera rotation: relative_x rotates yaw (negative = look left, positive = look right), relative_y rotates pitch (negative = look up, positive = look down). Typical values: 200-400px for a ~90° turn. Use navigate_to tool to calculate exact relative_x needed to face a target.

x.description: Absolute X position in viewport (for UI interaction)

y.description: Absolute Y position in viewport (for UI interaction)

relative_x.description: Relative X movement in pixels. For 3D camera: negative = look left, positive = look right. ~400px ≈ 180° turn

relative_y.description: Relative Y movement in pixels. For 3D camera: negative = look up, positive = look down

button_mask.description: Mouse button mask to simulate drag. 1=left button held, 2=right button held, 4=middle button held. Required for drag operations like camera pan. (default: 0)

unhandled.description: Force event to bypass GUI layer and go directly to _unhandled_input(). Auto-enabled when button_mask > 0. Use for camera pan/drag when UI overlays consume mouse events. (default: false)

tools.name: simulate_action
tools.description: Simulate a Godot Input Action (e.g. 'jump', 'move_left') in the running game

action.description: Action name as defined in Input Map (e.g. 'jump', 'move_left')

pressed.description: true for press, false for release (default: true)

tools.name: simulate_sequence
tools.description: Simulate a sequence of input events with optional frame delays between them. Useful for complex input patterns like press W → wait 30 frames → press Space → wait → release all. After the sequence, use capture_frames to verify the visual result.

button_mask.description: Mouse button mask for mouse_motion drag: 1=left, 2=right, 4=middle

unhandled.description: Bypass GUI, send directly to _unhandled_input. Auto-enabled for mouse_motion with button_mask > 0

events.description: Array of input events to send

frame_delay.description: Frames to wait between events (default: 1, 0 = all in one frame)

tools.name: get_game_scene_tree
tools.description: Get the scene tree of the currently running game (requires a scene to be playing). Supports filtering by script path, node type, or name.

max_depth.description: Maximum tree depth (-1 for unlimited, default: -1)

script_filter.description: Only include nodes whose script path contains this string (e.g. 'enemy' matches 'enemy.gd', 'enemy_drone.gd')

type_filter.description: Only include nodes of this Godot class (e.g. 'CharacterBody2D', 'Area2D')

named_only.description: If true, exclude nodes with auto-generated names (names starting with '@'). Default: false

tools.name: get_game_node_properties
tools.description: Get properties of a node in the running game (requires a scene to be playing)

node_path.description: Absolute node path in the running game (e.g. '/root/Main/Player')

properties.description: Specific property names to read (default: all editor-visible properties)

tools.name: set_game_node_property
tools.description: Set a property on a node in the running game (requires a scene to be playing). Useful for live-tweaking values like position, speed, health, etc.

node_path.description: Absolute node path in the running game (e.g. '/root/Main/Player')

value.description: Value to set. Accepts: strings with auto-parsing ('Vector2(100,200)', '#ff0000'), numbers, booleans, or JSON objects for vectors/colors ({"x":5,"y":3,"z":10} for Vector3, {"x":100,"y":200} for Vector2, {"r":1,"g":0,"b":0,"a":1} for Color)

tools.name: execute_game_script
tools.description: Execute arbitrary GDScript code inside the running game process. Use _mcp_print() to output values. Has access to the live scene tree and all game nodes.

code.description: GDScript code to execute in the running game. Use _mcp_print(value) to capture output. Code runs inside a run() function with access to the live game scene tree.

tools.name: capture_frames
tools.description: Capture multiple screenshots at regular frame intervals from the running game. Returns base64 PNG images. Use this to verify animations are playing correctly — if character poses differ across frames, the animation is working; if all frames show the same pose (e.g. T-pose), animation loading failed. Also useful for verifying movement, physics, and any time-based behavior. Prefer this over get_game_screenshot when you need to confirm something is changing over time.

count.description: Number of frames to capture (1-30, default: 5)

frame_interval.description: Frames to wait between captures (default: 10, i.e. ~6 captures/sec at 60fps)

half_resolution.description: Halve resolution to reduce data size (default: true)

node_data.description: Optional: capture node property data alongside each frame for debugging (position, velocity, etc.)

node_path.description: Path to a node to track (e.g. '/root/Main/Player')

properties.description: Property names to capture per frame (e.g. ['global_position', 'velocity'])

tools.name: record_frames
tools.description: Record many screenshots to files on disk for long-running debug observation. Unlike capture_frames (which returns base64 images directly), this saves PNG files to user://mcp_recorded_frames/ and returns file paths. Use this when you need more than 30 frames or want to observe behavior over a longer period without flooding the context with image data.

count.description: Number of frames to capture (1-600, default: 30)

frame_interval.description: Frames to wait between captures (default: 10, i.e. ~6 captures/sec at 60fps)

half_resolution.description: Halve resolution to reduce file size (default: true)

node_data.description: Optional: capture node property data alongside each frame for debugging

node_path.description: Path to a node to track (e.g. '/root/Main/Player')

properties.description: Property names to capture per frame (e.g. ['global_position', 'velocity'])

tools.name: monitor_properties
tools.description: Record property values over multiple frames from the running game. Returns a timeline of samples. Great for verifying movement (position changing), animation state (current_animation property), physics behavior (velocity), and debugging time-dependent issues.

node_path.description: Absolute node path in the running game (e.g. '/root/Main/Player')

frame_count.description: Number of samples to collect (1-600, default: 60)

frame_interval.description: Frames to wait between samples (default: 1, every frame)

tools.name: watch_signals
tools.description: Monitor signal emissions on specified nodes in the running game for a duration. Returns a timestamped log of every signal fired — great for debugging event flow, verifying signal connections, and understanding runtime behavior.

signal_filter.description: Only watch signals containing these substrings (e.g. ['health', 'died']). Omit to watch all signals.

duration_ms.description: How long to watch in milliseconds (500-30000, default: 5000)

tools.name: start_recording
tools.description: Start recording all input events (keyboard, mouse, actions) in the running game. Use stop_recording to get the recorded events.

tools.name: stop_recording
tools.description: Stop recording input events and return the recorded event timeline. Events include timestamps for replay.

tools.name: replay_recording
tools.description: Replay a previously recorded input event sequence in the running game. Useful for regression testing — record a test once, replay it after code changes.

events.description: Array of recorded event objects (from stop_recording output)

tools.name: find_nodes_by_script
tools.description: Find all nodes in the running game whose script path contains a given string. Returns matching nodes with their properties.

script.description: Script path substring to search for (e.g. 'enemy', 'player.gd')

properties.description: Specific property names to include for each match (default: all editor-visible properties)

tools.name: get_autoload
tools.description: Get properties of an autoload/singleton node in the running game. Quick access to global game state like GameManager, EventBus, etc.

properties.description: Specific property names to read (default: all editor-visible properties)

tools.name: find_ui_elements
tools.description: Find all visible UI elements (Button, Label, LineEdit, CheckBox, Slider, etc.) in the running game. Returns each element's text, type, position, and center point for clicking.

type_filter.description: Only return elements of this type (e.g. 'Button', 'Label', 'CheckBox'). Default: all types

tools.name: click_button_by_text
tools.description: Click a button in the running game by its text label. Finds the button, calculates its center, and simulates a full click (press + release). Much easier than manual coordinate-based clicking.

text.description: Button text to search for (e.g. 'New Game', 'Start', 'OK')

partial.description: Allow partial text matching (default: true). If false, requires exact match.

tools.name: wait_for_node
tools.description: Wait until a node exists at the given path in the running game scene tree. Useful for waiting after scene transitions, node spawning, or UI state changes.

node_path.description: Absolute node path to wait for (e.g. '/root/Main/Player', '/root/Dungeon')

poll_frames.description: Frames between each check (default: 5, i.e. ~12 checks/sec at 60fps)

tools.name: find_nearby_nodes
tools.description: Find all nodes within a radius of a position in the running game, sorted by distance. Useful for finding what's near the player (collectibles, enemies, interactables) without manually querying each node's position.

position.description: Origin position: either a node_path string (e.g. '/root/Main/Player') to use that node's global_position, or an {x, y, z} coordinate object

type_filter.description: Only include nodes of this Godot class (e.g. 'Area3D', 'CharacterBody3D')

group_filter.description: Only include nodes in this group (e.g. 'enemies', 'collectibles')

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10)

tools.name: navigate_to
tools.description: Calculate navigation info from the player to a target in the running 3D game. Returns the world direction, camera-relative suggested WASD keys to press, camera yaw rotation needed (as mouse relative_x pixels for simulate_mouse_move), and estimated walk duration. Use this to plan movement instead of manually calculating directions.

target.description: Target: either a node_path string (e.g. '/root/Main/Crystal') or an {x, y, z} coordinate object

camera_path.description: Camera node path (default: auto-detect active Camera3D)

move_speed.description: Player movement speed in units/sec for duration estimation (default: 5.0)

tools.name: move_to
tools.description: Autopilot the player character to walk to a target position in the running 3D game. Handles camera rotation and forward movement internally at 60fps — completes in a single call with no manual simulate_key/simulate_mouse_move loops needed. The player's camera pivot is directly rotated toward the target, and W key is injected to walk. Much more reliable and efficient than navigate_to + manual input simulation.

target.description: Target: either a node_path string (e.g. '/root/Main/Crystal') or an {x, y, z} coordinate object

camera_path.description: Camera pivot node path (default: auto-detect SpringArm3D child of player, or active Camera3D parent)

arrival_radius.description: Stop when this close to target in world units (default: 1.5)

run.description: Hold Shift for running speed (default: false)

look_at_target.description: Rotate camera toward target while moving (default: true). Set false to walk forward without turning.

tools.name: batch_get_properties
tools.description: Get properties of multiple nodes at once in the running game. More efficient than calling get_game_node_properties multiple times.

properties.description: Specific properties to read (default: all editor-visible)

tools.name: get_input_actions
tools.description: Get all input actions defined in the project's Input Map with their key/button bindings

filter.description: Filter action names containing this substring

tools.name: set_input_action
tools.description: Create or update an input action with key/mouse/joypad bindings. Saves to project.godot and updates the runtime InputMap.

button_index.description: Button index for mouse/joypad button types

axis_value.description: Axis value (-1.0 or 1.0) for joypad_motion type

tools.name: setup_collision
tools.description: Add a CollisionShape2D/3D child to a physics body or area node with a specified shape. Auto-detects 2D/3D from the parent node type.

node_path.description: Path to the parent physics body or area node (e.g. CharacterBody2D, StaticBody3D, Area2D)

shape.description: Shape type: 'rectangle'/'rect', 'circle', 'capsule', 'segment' (2D only), 'cylinder' (3D only), 'custom'/'convex'. For 3D: 'box'/'sphere' also work.

width.description: Width for rectangle/box shape (default: 32 for 2D, 1 for 3D)

points.description: Convex polygon points as [[x,y],...] for 2D or [[x,y,z],...] for 3D

disabled.description: Create the collision shape disabled (default: false)

one_way_collision.description: Enable one-way collision (2D only, default: false)

tools.name: set_physics_layers
tools.description: Set collision layer and/or mask on a physics body or area node. Supports bitmask integers or arrays of layer numbers.

node_path.description: Path to the node with collision layers

collision_layer.description: Collision layer: bitmask integer or array of layer numbers [1,3,5]

collision_mask.description: Collision mask: bitmask integer or array of layer numbers [1,2,4]

tools.name: get_physics_layers
tools.description: Get the current collision layer and mask for a node, including named layer info from ProjectSettings.

node_path.description: Path to the node with collision layers

tools.name: add_raycast
tools.description: Add a RayCast2D/3D child node for collision detection. Auto-detects 2D/3D from the parent node type.

hit_from_inside.description: Detect hits from inside shapes (default: false)

tools.name: setup_physics_body
tools.description: Configure physics body properties. For CharacterBody2D/3D: floor settings, motion mode, etc. For RigidBody2D/3D: mass, gravity, damping, etc.

node_path.description: Path to the physics body node

floor_stop_on_slope.description: CharacterBody: stop on slopes when not moving

floor_max_angle.description: CharacterBody: maximum floor angle in radians (default ~0.785 = 45 degrees)

floor_snap_length.description: CharacterBody: floor snap distance for sticking to the ground

wall_min_slide_angle.description: CharacterBody: minimum angle for wall sliding in radians

freeze.description: RigidBody: freeze the body (stop physics simulation)

contact_monitor.description: RigidBody: enable contact monitoring for body_entered/body_exited signals

max_contacts_reported.description: RigidBody: max contacts to report (requires contact_monitor)

tools.name: get_collision_info
tools.description: Get detailed collision information for a node: all collision shapes, layers/masks, raycasts, and physics body settings. Scans children by default.

node_path.description: Path to the node to inspect

include_children.description: Include children in the scan (default: true)

tools.name: create_animation_tree
tools.description: Create an AnimationTree node with an AnimationNodeStateMachine as root, optionally linked to an AnimationPlayer

node_path.description: Path to the parent node where the AnimationTree will be added

anim_player.description: Relative path from the AnimationTree to the AnimationPlayer (e.g. '../AnimationPlayer')

tools.name: get_animation_tree_structure
tools.description: Read the full structure of an AnimationTree including all states, transitions, and blend tree nodes

tools.name: add_state_machine_state
tools.description: Add a state to an AnimationNodeStateMachine (animation clip, blend tree, or nested state machine)

animation.description: Animation name to play (only for state_type='animation')

state_machine_path.description: Slash-separated path to a nested state machine (e.g. 'Run/SubState'). Empty or omit for root.

position_x.description: X position in the graph editor (default: 0)

position_y.description: Y position in the graph editor (default: 0)

tools.name: remove_state_machine_state
tools.description: Remove a state from an AnimationNodeStateMachine (also removes connected transitions)

state_name.description: Name of the state to remove

state_machine_path.description: Slash-separated path to a nested state machine. Empty or omit for root.

tools.name: add_state_machine_transition
tools.description: Add a transition between two states in an AnimationNodeStateMachine with configurable switch mode, advance mode, and expression conditions

from_state.description: Source state name (use 'Start' for the entry point)

to_state.description: Destination state name (use 'End' for the exit point)

advance_expression.description: GDScript expression that triggers this transition (e.g. 'is_running')

state_machine_path.description: Slash-separated path to a nested state machine. Empty or omit for root.

tools.name: remove_state_machine_transition
tools.description: Remove a transition between two states in an AnimationNodeStateMachine

state_machine_path.description: Slash-separated path to a nested state machine. Empty or omit for root.

tools.name: set_blend_tree_node
tools.description: Add or replace a node inside an AnimationNodeBlendTree state (Add2, Blend2, TimeScale, Animation, etc.) with optional connection

blend_tree_state.description: Name of the BlendTree state in the state machine

bt_node_name.description: Name for the node inside the BlendTree

bt_node_type.description: Type of BlendTree node to create

connect_to.description: Name of another BlendTree node to connect this node's output to

connect_port.description: Input port index on the target node (default: 0)

state_machine_path.description: Slash-separated path to a nested state machine. Empty or omit for root.

position_x.description: X position in the graph editor (default: 0)

position_y.description: Y position in the graph editor (default: 0)

tools.name: set_tree_parameter
tools.description: Set an AnimationTree parameter value (conditions, blend amounts, time scale, etc.)

parameter.description: Parameter path (e.g. 'conditions/is_running', 'Blend2/blend_amount'). 'parameters/' prefix is auto-added if missing.

value.description: Parameter value. Strings are auto-parsed for Vector2, Color, etc.

tools.name: setup_navigation_region

tools.name: run_test_scenario
tools.description: Execute a test scenario in the running game. Optionally plays a scene, then runs a sequence of steps (input simulation, waits, assertions, screenshots). Returns pass/fail summary. Note: keep scenarios short (under 20 seconds total) to avoid timeout.

scene_path.description: Scene to play before running steps. Use 'main' for main scene, 'current' for current scene, or a res:// path. If omitted, uses already-running scene.

steps.description: Array of test steps. Each step has a 'type' field: 'input' (action/keycode simulation), 'wait' (seconds or node_path to wait for), 'assert' (node_path+property+expected+operator, or text for screen text), 'screenshot' (capture a frame). Examples: {type:'input', action:'ui_accept'}, {type:'wait', seconds:0.5}, {type:'wait', node_path:'/root/Main/Player'}, {type:'assert', node_path:'/root/Main/Player', property:'health', expected:100, operator:'eq'}, {type:'assert', text:'Game Over'}, {type:'screenshot'}

tools.name: assert_node_state
tools.description: Assert a node's property value in the running game. Compares the actual property value against an expected value using the specified operator. Returns pass/fail with actual value for debugging.

node_path.description: Absolute node path in the running game (e.g. '/root/Main/Player')

operator.description: Comparison operator (default: 'eq'). eq/neq: equality, gt/lt/gte/lte: numeric comparison, contains: string/array contains, type_is: check Godot type name

tools.name: assert_screen_text
tools.description: Assert that specific text is visible on screen in the running game. Searches all visible UI elements (Button, Label, LineEdit, etc.) for matching text. Useful for verifying UI state, dialog content, or game messages.

text.description: Text to search for on screen (e.g. 'Game Over', 'Score:', 'New Game')

partial.description: Allow partial text matching (default: true). If false, requires exact match.

tools.name: run_stress_test
tools.description: Run rapid random input events for a specified duration and check if the game crashes. Sends random UI actions (up/down/left/right/accept/cancel) plus any custom actions. Returns whether the game survived, event count, and new errors.

duration.description: Duration in seconds to run the stress test (1-60, default: 5)

actions.description: Additional input action names to include in random input pool (e.g. ['jump', 'attack', 'dash'])

tools.name: get_test_report
tools.description: Collect and format results from all assertions run so far (via assert_node_state, assert_screen_text, and run_test_scenario) into a summary test report. Shows pass/fail counts, pass rate, and detailed results.

clear.description: Clear accumulated results after generating report (default: true)
